column1: # comment: "Deception / falsehood / misinformation alignments. FORMAL GROUNDING: gmeow:heldStandpoint / gmeow:projectedStandpoint realise the divergence model of deception as standpoint-indexed claims; gmeow:bullshit is the Frankfurt modality integrated into the Standpoint-Logic value space. schema.org: ClaimReview is an attestation act (not a truth verdict); Rating is a lossy projection to VerificationResult. CRMinf: I6_Belief_Value aligns to gmeow:StandpointModality (including the bullshit modality); I1_Argumentation is referenced for the solver-layer argument-acceptability function. PROV-O: deception events are prov:Activity; standpoint claims are prov:Entity. Wikidata: wd:Q170028 (deception) aligns to gmeow:eventTypeDeception. AIF (Argument Interchange Format) is referenced in the solver layer (fnArgumentAcceptability) but not aligned via TermEquivalence because AIF lacks a stable, resolvable RDF namespace suitable for SSSOM rows."

column6: comment
a deception event is a provenance activity; the specific deception semantics are GMEOW-specific and not entailed by PROV-O
a standpoint claim (held or projected) is a provenance entity attributed to its standpoint agent
GMEOW's StandpointModality (unequivocal/probable/conceivable/refuted/bullshit) spans and extends CRMinf's I6 Belief Value
an attribution of deceptive intent is an argumentation act in the CRMinf sense; acceptability is computed externally (Principle 12)
Frankfurt's essay 'On Bullshit' (Q1760159) — the philosophical source of the bullshit modality. Related rather than close match because the item is a literary work, not the concept itself.

Wikidata 'bullshit' (Q2063516) — the general vulgar term, not specifically Frankfurt's philosophical concept. Related rather than close match because the item is the broad term, not the indifference-to-truth modality.
Wikidata 'deception' (Q170028) — the act of propagating beliefs that are not true

Wikidata 'disinformation' (Q189656) — false information spread deliberately to deceive. GMEOW models this as eventTypeDisinformation: a coordinated propagated deception where the originating node carries held≠projected divergence + deceptive intent, and unwitting reshares become misinformation at their local node.

Wikidata 'fake news' (Q28549308) — a type of yellow journalism or propaganda that consists of deliberate disinformation or hoaxes spread via traditional print and broadcast news media or online social media. Related match because fake news is a media-format instance of disinformation, not the general concept.

Wikidata 'propaganda' (Q7281) — information, especially of a biased or misleading nature, used to promote a political cause or point of view. Related rather than close match because propaganda may be true or false; disinformation is specifically false and deceptive.
Wikidata 'rumor' (Q878352) — a circulating story of uncertain origin. Related rather than close match because a rumor may be true, false, or unverified; disinformation is deliberately false.

Wikidata 'spin' (Q12776523) — a form of propaganda, achieved through providing an interpretation of an event or campaign to persuade public opinion. GMEOW generalises this to eventTypeDistortion covering all sharpening/re-framing deceptions.

Wikidata 'forgery' (Q1332286) — the generic concept shared with eventTypeForgery. Close match for fabrication at lower confidence because fabrication invents without mimicking a specific genuine work.

Wikidata 'tampering with evidence' (Q18387855) — the act of altering or fabricating evidence to mislead. GMEOW models this as eventTypeFabrication: a false CreativeWork whose attested provenance is refuted.

Wikidata 'forgery' (Q1332286) — the act of fabricating or imitating a document, signature, currency, or work of art with intent to deceive. GMEOW models this as eventTypeForgery: a fabrication with a counterpartOf link to the genuine work and a failed cryptographic signature verification.
Wikidata 'document forgery' (Q693988) — a specific form of forgery involving official or personal documents. GMEOW models this as eventTypeForgery with the same structural machinery.

Wikidata 'impersonation' (Q2146099) — the act of pretending to be another person. GMEOW models this as eventTypeImpersonation: a projected identity claim whose facetSubject differs from the deceiver. Phishing and spoofing are instances, never taxonomy primitives.
Wikidata 'lie' (Q4925193) — a false statement made with deliberate intent to deceive. GMEOW models this as eventTypeLie with held standpoint refuted and projected standpoint unequivocal.
Wikidata 'self-deception' (Q1602343) — the process of denying or rationalising away the relevance, significance, or importance of opposing evidence and logical argument.

Wikidata 'misinformation' (Q13579947) — false or inaccurate information regardless of intent. GMEOW models misinformation structurally: a claim tagged veridicalityUntrue with no held≠projected divergence and no deceptiveIntentClaim at the local node. The boundary is per-node, not global.

schema:ClaimReview is a fact-checking act; in GMEOW it is an Attestation with attestationTypeFactCheck. The single-verdict model of ClaimReview is a lossy projection — GMEOW keeps every standpoint's assessment as a coexisting claim.
schema:Rating (the outcome of a ClaimReview) projects to gmeow:VerificationResult — a lossy downcast dropping the standpoint axis and confidence.
